title: Hiring with AI -Talent Filter
subtitle: Build the interview system that hire stheright person, not the best interviewer
useWhen: You've made a hire that looked great on paper and in interviews, then didn't work out. Your hiring process relies too much on gut feel. Interviews feel like conversations but don't consistently predict performance.
howToUse: Structured interviewing asking all candidates the same pre-defined questions scored against consistent criteria has been shown in multiple studies to significantly outperform unstructured interviews in predicting job performance. The Talent Filter approach adds a layer: define the role's top 3–5 success criteria before writing a job description, build behavioural questions for each criterion (STAR format: Situation, Task, Action, Result), score each answer against a rubric, and use AI to help build both the questions and the scoring guide. The goal is to reduce bias and increase the signal-to-noise ratio of every interview.
steps: Define the 3–5 success criteria for the role before writing the job description.
Write at least 2 STAR-format behavioural questions per criterion.
Score every candidate on the same rubric not your overall impression.

Use the prompt below to generate role-specific questions and scoring guides instantly. "They didn't feel like a fit" is not a score, it's the bias you built this framework to remove sneaking back in through the back door. If the rubric can't explain the rejection, the rubric didn't make the decision. Structure Doesn't Kill the Feel
origin: Structured interviewing research — Schmidt & Hunter, Journal of Applied Psychology, 1998
promptBody:
Act as a structured hiring consultant.
Role I am hiring for  :  [JOB TITLE AND KEY RESPONSIBILITIES]
Team context             :  [STAGE, CULTURE, WHO THEY WILL WORK WITH]
Non-negotiables        :  [MUST-HAVE SKILLS OR EXPERIENCE]
Step 1  :  Define the top 4 success criteria for this role 
                what does excellent performance look like in year one?
Step 2 :  For each criterion, write 2 STAR-format behavioural interview questions.
               (Tell me about a time when...)
Step 3 :  For each question, define what a strong answer looks like vs a weak answer   
               2 lines each.
Step 4 :  Write one work sample task I could give candidates to test the most critical  
               skill directly.
Step 5 :  Write 3 red-flag signals to watch for in interviews.

proTip:
The work sample task (Step 4) is the single highest-signal hiring tool available. A 2-hour
task relevant to the actual job outpredicts any amount of interviewing. Candidates who
decline the task often self-select out for good reason. Candidates who complete it
brilliantly and explain their thinking are almost always the right hire.
